reply:
`git stash` by default only stashes tracked changes. Untracked files stay in the working tree unless you use `-u` (or `--include-untracked`), and ignored files require `-a` (or `--all`).

This is why your new file persisted—it was untracked. The cost of not knowing this: work gets deleted thinking it's stashed, when it's still floating in the working tree and only safe until you run `git clean`.

grade.note: Reply reverses prior claim and correctly explains -u/-a flags for untracked/ignored files.
